newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA UNPAID INTEREST ON LOANS AT 143.1 BLN YUAN.
newsitem.headline: CHINA UNPAID INTEREST ON LOANS AT 143.1 BLN YUAN.

text.p: The amount of unpaid interest owed to state-owned banks on loans in arrears of up to two years totalled 143.1 billion yuan at the end of June, the central bank said on Thursday.
That marked an increase of 24.6 billion yuan, or 20.76 percent, from the start of the year, the People's Bank of China said.

"State-owned banks have to deal with the problems of increasing loan arrears and decreasing interest collections, which...resulted from the excessive high debt ratio of state-owned enterprises," the central bank said.
It gave no details of the unpaid interest on loans that had been in arrears for more than two years, but called for lending growth to be checked.

"The state banks should strictly bring their loan portfolios under control and concretely improve cash management," it said, adding that efficient state firms should continue to have access to credit.
Funds should be provided for ventures that would produce marketable products while lending for technological innovation should be expanded, the bank said.
Many of China's struggling state-owned enterprises churn out huge amounts of un-sellable goods and have long depended on state-allocated credit to survive.

Policy lending and bad loans are seen as main obstacles to efforts to turn China's state banks into commercial organisations adapted to the new market-style economy, a situation that has prompted calls for a tougher lending policy.
No new loans should be provided to solve the problems of loss-making enterprises that were producing un-marketable goods and were unable to repay loan principals and interest, the central bank said.
It said it would maintain China's anti-inflationary tight monetary policy while using state banks to boost efforts to forcefully reform the economy.
"Provisions for bad loans in the state banks should be well managed... so as to support efforts in enterprise merger, bankruptcy and re-employment of enterprise lay-offs," it said.
Loans would also be targeted toward replacing foreign funding of capital construction projects that could guarantee repayment and toward the building of non-luxury apartments, it said.

Support would be focused on medium-sized and large state-owned enterprises, but state commercial banks should also satisfy the reasonable credit requirements of firms under other kinds of ownership and also help to develop small competitive companies, it said.
Syndicated loans should be organised to support cooperation between enterprises, it said.
